channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Trump says the FBI is "looking into" Jensen Huang's affair, and the Nvidia CEO told him he "had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy" (Associated Press)
item.description: Donald Trump claimed that the FBI is investigating an espionage-related matter involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang reportedly defended himself by stating he had no idea the person involved was a spy, as the investigation unfolds.

item.title: Jensen Huang's affair shines a spotlight on Nvidia's weak board and opaque succession planning at what has become the world's most important company (Semafor)
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is mired in scandal following reports of an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset, raising serious questions about governance and security. As the architect of Nvidia's dominance, Huang's extreme management style—maintaining over 50 direct reports—has left the company with no clear succession plan and a weak board, exposing the firm to massive operational risks.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead just before its IPO
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 ahead of its IPO, offering significant performance gains and reduced API pricing. The Fable model prioritizes general safety, while Mythos lifts specific restrictions for verified cybersecurity and life sciences organizations.

item.title: AI infrastructure provider Fireworks says hackers accessed some customers' datasets, incomplete model weights, and billing information over the past month (Anna Tong/Forbes)
item.description: AI infrastructure provider Fireworks suffered a security breach, allowing hackers to access customers' datasets, partial model weights, and billing info over the past month. Several major clients are already migrating their operations elsewhere.

item.title: SpaceX plans a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, TX, with ~$24B of investment for initial phases, per a public hearing notice (Bloomberg)
item.description: SpaceX has submitted a public notice to construct a gas-fired power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas. With an initial investment of approximately $24 billion, the project aims to provide dedicated power and extreme computing performance for aerospace missions.

item.title: Anthropic prices Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 at $8/1M input and $40/1M output tokens, down 20% from 5.1; fast mode costs $16/1M input and $80/1M output tokens (Frederic Lardinois/The New Stack)
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, cutting prices by 20% compared to version 5.1. The company also introduced a 'Fast Mode' option, which is priced significantly higher than the standard tier.

item.title: Meta launches Muse Ember, a small AI model built for the repetitive work agents actually do
item.description: Meta has launched Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient AI model designed for routine agent tasks like tool calling and document processing. The model prioritizes cost-efficiency, aiming to dominate the AI agent market with a significantly lower price-per-task compared to existing industry rivals.

item.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
item.description: A critical Linux vulnerability dubbed *sshole is currently under active exploitation. The flaw, stemming from the interaction between OpenSSH and the musl library, allows unauthorized root-level access. Threat actors have already begun compromising servers in Southeast Asia and planting backdoors.

item.title: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
item.description: Amid growing public backlash against data centers in the US, Big Tech often frames the issue as a proxy for broader cultural anxieties. However, evidence suggests the root cause is a pragmatic conflict over power grid capacity and the massive electricity demands of AI infrastructure.

item.title: Anthropic says during prerelease testing Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2 formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem and solved two open black hole physics problems (Jay Peters/The Verge)
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, featuring enhanced reasoning and coding capabilities. The models have reportedly formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem and solved complex black hole physics problems, aiming to tackle daunting technical challenges with higher efficiency.

item.title: Apple’s $50 Intelligence Usage Packs extend access to some AI features
item.description: based AI features. This move marks the first time Apple has monetized specific AI usage within an app to offset costs associated with third-party models from OpenAI and Google.

item.title: Anthropic releases Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2, saying they are "best for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work", for $8/1M input and $40/1M output tokens (Anthropic)
item.description: We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges. Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. item.title: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
item.description: Anthropic has officially launched the Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models, designed to tackle daunting technical challenges. These versions feature significant improvements in coding, logic, and vision with increased speed, reportedly solving complex scientific problems like black hole physics.

item.title: ChatGPT Enterprise now available in AWS Marketplace
item.description: OpenAI has made ChatGPT Enterprise available on the AWS Marketplace, allowing organizations to procure the service through existing AWS billing relationships. This move streamlines the procurement process for enterprise clients and accelerates OpenAI's integration into cloud service ecosystems.

item.title: Mavria, which aims to build modular data centers that can be shipped by trucks, raised $130M across pre-seed and seed rounds at a $1B valuation led by Paradigm (Jennifer Hiller/Wall Street Journal)
item.description: Mavria has raised $130 million across several rounds, achieving a $1 billion valuation to build modular data centers capable of being transported by truck. The company aims to address the urgent demand for flexible AI infrastructure deployment.

item.title: Bytedance's Seedream 5.5 promises pixel-stable image editing across 100 rounds without color drift
item.description: Bytedance has introduced the Seedream 5.5 image generation model, tailored for professional workflows. Its key features include stable multi-round editing for up to 100 rounds without color shift and native RGBA transparent background generation, now rolling out across their product suite.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Ember, its smallest and most cost-efficient AI model yet, saying it delivers more intelligence per dollar than Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna (Russell Brandom/TechCrunch)
item.description: Meta's Superintelligence Lab has released Muse Ember, a lightweight model optimized for high-frequency agent tasks like tool calls, coding, and document parsing. By offering a significantly lower cost of 10 cents per million input tokens, it challenges competitors like Haiku and Luna to capture the market for large-scale, cost-efficient agentic workflows.

item.title: Instagram’s Effect Builder makes new filters from AI prompts
item.description: Instagram has launched the Effect Builder, allowing adult users in the US to create custom filters using text prompts. Users can describe their ideas or upload reference images, with the system optimizing prompts to generate the effects for direct submission.

item.title: The future of AI hinges on… Jensen Huang’s sex life?
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is under fire following reports of an affair with former reporter Alice Huang. Her company, Megaspeed, made a sudden, massive $4.8 billion purchase of Nvidia chips, raising alarms as intelligence reports suggest she acted as a honeypot for China’s MSS to gain access to sensitive commercial and potentially political communication.

item.title: Uber launches Uber Parking, an in-app parking reservation tool powered by its SpotHero acquisition, in 15 US cities, including Chicago, NYC, and San Francisco (Andrew J. Hawkins/The Verge)
item.description: Uber has integrated SpotHero technology to launch an in-app parking reservation tool across 15 US cities. The feature allows users to search, book, and pay for parking spots, utilizing QR codes or license plate recognition to manage the parking experience directly within the Uber ecosystem.

item.title: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
item.description: California State Senator Scott Wiener, having won the congressional seat vacated by Nancy Pelosi, has prioritized AI regulation. Citing new reports on recursive self-improvement in AI, he criticized Congress for its slow pace and demanded urgent federal legislation to mitigate existential risks.

item.title: French officials say Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the cyberattacks that knocked out commercial refrigerators and freezers across France in October (Reuters)
item.description: French officials have accused the Iranian Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks in October that disabled commercial refrigerators and freezers across France. These attacks disrupted retail cold chains, sparking significant concerns regarding the vulnerability of critical national infrastructure.

item.title: Disney bets on Adobe's Firefly to create brand-safe AI models for its entertainment empire
item.description: Disney announced a multi-year partnership with Adobe at the MAX conference, utilizing Adobe's Firefly Foundry to train custom AI models embedded with its core IP. Driven by divisions like Imagineering and ESPN Edge, the project aims to integrate production-ready, brand-safe generative tools into theme park development, film production, and sports content creation.

item.title: Sources: a Commerce Department investigation into Megaspeed for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China was transferred to the DOJ after Nvidia intervened (New York Times)
item.description: Singapore-based Megaspeed is under fire for allegedly smuggling Nvidia's high-end A-series chips into China. Following Nvidia's intervention and cooperation, the Commerce Department has escalated the case to the Department of Justice, signaling a shift from administrative probe to criminal investigation.

item.title: An interview with ex-Shein Executive Chair Donald Tang who insists it was his decision to step down ahead of the troubled IPO, Shein's valuation rout, and more (Patrick Jenkins/Financial Times)
item.description: Former Shein Executive Chair Donald Tang broke his silence on his resignation, insisting it was his personal decision rather than being pushed out. Amid the company's stalled IPO and valuation rout, Tang's move aims to distance himself from the deepening organizational turmoil and market skepticism.

item.title: Trump’s 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
item.description: Donald Trump claimed during a televised interview that he once threatened a prominent AI executive with jail time over dangerous activities. He asserted this intimidation forced the executive to change everything, using the anecdote to argue that AI risks are manageable under government oversight.

item.title: Tencent's AI chief says AI bioweapons are coming, but closing off models isn't the answer
item.description: Tencent AI scientist Yao Shunyu warns that AI's potential for bioweapon development, combined with blurred lines between offense and defense, makes neither full open-source nor closed-source models a silver bullet. Citing the Hugging Face incident, he advocates for a nuanced middle ground to balance utility and risk.

item.title: Draft law: the EU's Digital Fairness Act would require companies to let adults disable addictive features and will target AI bots that simulate relationships (Bloomberg)
item.description: The EU is drafting the 'Digital Fairness Act' to crack down on addictive platform designs, mandating that companies provide users with the option to disable such features. The legislation also specifically targets AI chatbots that simulate human relationships to mitigate psychological dependency.

item.title: Disney and Adobe are building generative AI tools together
item.description: Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed. The multiyear partnership was announced today at Adobe’s MAX

item.title: Hold up — I had a great time talking to the RIAA guy
item.description: Mitch Glazier, CEO of the RIAA, stated that copyright owners, artists, and the public share a growing resentment toward unauthorized AI data scraping. The discussion focused on legal complexities of deepfakes and the urgent need for standardized AI labeling and detection systems on major distribution platforms.
